messages:
Maya (AE): FYI - Customer (MacroBank) wants a Private VPC POC. Constraints: strict egress allowlist (single /28), on-prem SD-WAN to AWS, and they reported truncated responses from our model (looks like MTU/gRPC). Can we do this without changing their perimeter rules?
Omar (Solutions Eng): Short answer: maybe. Two paths: 1) PrivateLink (interface endpoint) to our connector in their VPC, or 2) VPC peering / TGW to a Redwood-managed VPC. PrivateLink + NLB generally keeps traffic local to their AZ and avoids peering IP conflicts.
Liam (NetOps): Note on IPs: PrivateLink ENIs are in-customer subnets with private IPs so app->ENI preserves srcIP at the VPC level. But our control-plane egress still comes from our public EIPs for telemetry/metrics unless they host the connector fully in their account. If procurement insists on a single /28 allowlist we need to give them specific EIPs to allow.
Priya (NetSec): MTU/gRPC: typical symptom is MSS clamping needed when there's an SD-WAN or VPN with lower MTU. If packets exceed path MTU you get truncation or reset. Ask their network team if their IPSEC/SD-WAN uses 1400 MTU. We can work around with keepalive/fragmentation or enable TCP MSS clamping on the connector.
Omar (Solutions Eng): Example workaround (quick): configure the connector host to clamp MSS to 1360. If they're using managed NLB we can also recommend ALB/gRPC + proxy with correct proxy protocol.
Liam (NetOps): Quick snippet for infra team (iptables MSS clamp):

iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu

Liam (NetOps): Also: if they insist on our connector SNATing to a specific EIP, we can offer a fixed egress EIP set (support ticket + onboarding) but that requires us to centralize outbound from our infra so won't preserve original client IP to their app logs. Tradeoff.
Maya (AE): Procurement also asked if PrivateLink avoids cross-account route table changes (they hate touching routes). Any clear line to give them?
Omar (Solutions Eng): PrivateLink minimal route changes: they just create interface endpoints (ENIs auto-created) and update SGs. No peering routes. VPC peering/TGW requires route table entries and potentially CIDR rework. For quick POC, PrivateLink usually wins.
Priya (NetSec): Security questionnaire copy for "Network Requirements":

"Redwood Private deployment supports two patterns: (A) Connector-in-customer-VPC: the connector is deployed as a customer-managed resource and communicates outbound to Redwood control plane over TLS (443). Source IPs remain customer-origin due to in-VPC deployment. (B) PrivateLink: requires creation of an Interface VPC Endpoint; application traffic terminates on ENIs in-customer subnets. Firewall requirements: allow outbound TLS (443) to Redwood control plane EIP ranges (provided pre-onboarding) and allow inbound TLS (443) to connector ENIs if using interface endpoints. No inbound internet-facing exposure is required"

Maya (AE): Nice. They also want an infra example to paste into their runbook for SGs and a short checklist for onprem SD-WAN folks.
Liam (NetOps): SG example (allowlist minimal):

# Allow app subnet to reach connector ENIs
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-app --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.0.5.0/24
# Allow connector to reach control plane
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-connector --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 198.51.100.0/28

Liam (NetOps): Checklist for SD-WAN/Network team: 1) Confirm SD-WAN MTU or enable MSS clamping. 2) Allow outbound 443 to our control-plane EIPs (we'll give the /28). 3) If using PrivateLink, open SG from app->endpoint. 4) If preserving client srcIP, deploy connector in-customer VPC or use passthrough proxy.
Omar (Solutions Eng): Pricing/POC note: small POC (single AZ connector) is usually quoted with a one-time onboarding + month of connector hosting; large enterprise ask for HA across AZs raises infra line items. I'll prepare quick numbers after I grab the infra SKU.
infra-bot: POC workspace provisioned: redwood-poc-macrobank-1 (poc id pb-99aabb). Link: https://internal.redwood/pocs/pb-99aabb
Priya (NetSec): Also flag: if their compliance needs packet capture for audit, we need a discussion about log redaction and retention. I can own that questionnaire follow-up.
Maya (AE): Thanks team. I'll forward the copy-paste snippet + SG examples to their network/security leads and ask for SD-WAN MTU details. Please drop the EIP /28 and exact HA costs here once you have them.
Liam (NetOps): Will post EIP ranges + healthcheck TTL recs in ~1hr.
Omar (Solutions Eng): I'll draft a 1-slide diagram (PrivateLink vs in-VPC) and attach sample cost lines.
Priya (NetSec): Ping me if legal asks about TLS interception or key custody.
Maya (AE): Closing for now 389
